question: Assume today is 2026-09-08. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the total number of A&E attendances in England in September 2026 (all A&E types, including minor injury units and walk-in centres), as reported in NHS England's monthly A&E Attendances and Emergency Admissions statistics.

target.what: Total A&E attendances (all types: major type 1, single-specialty type 2, and other/minor injury units and walk-in centres type 3) recorded in England during September 2026, as reported in NHS England's monthly A&E Attendances and Emergency Admissions statistics (the 'A&E attendances' count, not emer
target.publisher: NHS England (NHS Digital / NHS England Performance Analysis Team), monthly A&E Attendances and Emergency Admissions statistics
target.cadence: monthly, published with roughly a 4-6 week lag after month end
target.caveats: Target period is entirely in the future relative to the 2026-09-08 cutoff, so no observed value exists; must be forecast from history plus current signals. Working interpretation: total attendances across all A&E types (type 1 + type 2 + type 3), England only, one calendar month, count of visits not

candidates.hypothesis: September 2026 attendances will follow the level and seasonal pattern of recent Septembers and the trailing 12 months; the most recent published months before cutoff (through ~June/July 2026) anchor the level, and a September seasonal factor (September vs recent-month ratio from prior years) projects forward. Target = recent monthly level * September seasonal index * trend adjustment.
candidates.data_to_find: Monthly total A&E attendances (all types) for England for each month from Jan 2023 through the latest month published before 2026-09-08; and September values for 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025 to derive a September-to-recent-month seasonal ratio. Minimum: latest 3-6 months plus 3 prior Septembers.

candidates.hypothesis: Total attendances = type 1 + type 2 + type 3. Type 1 dominates and is more stable; type 3 (MIU/WIC) has been declining. Estimating each component separately and summing reduces error versus a single aggregate trend. Target = sum over types of (recent type-level level * type-specific September factor).
candidates.data_to_find: Monthly attendances split by A&E type (type 1, type 2, type 3) for England for recent months and prior Septembers; shares of each type in total. Minimum: latest month type split plus one prior September split.

candidates.hypothesis: Monthly attendances = average daily attendances * number of days (30). Daily A&E attendance figures (published daily/weekly by NHS England during winter and in some dashboards) give a direct throughput rate; September 2026 has 30 days and specific weekday composition. Target = mean daily attendances in early September * 30, adjusted for weekday mix.
candidates.data_to_find: Daily or weekly total A&E attendances for England in recent weeks before cutoff (August-early September 2026 if available), and average daily attendances per month historically to convert to monthly. Minimum: a recent daily/weekly rate or a monthly total with day count.

methods.label: m1
methods.rationale: September 2025 total (p148) scaled by the most recent published YoY growth signal. p18 is July 2026 (+3.3%); p2 is April 2026 (+2.1%). Both are total-attendance YoY growth for 2026, so the signal series has a 2026 value; code takes the median of the 2026 signals. Shared dependency: all from NHS England monthly releases; failure mode is that mid-year growth may not carry into September.
notes: p2: period 2026-04-01..2026-04-30 is not the same calendar period as 2026-07-01..2026-07-31

methods.label: m2

p16.role: Total A&E attendances, England, July 2026 (all types), latest observed monthly level

a2.role: September-to-July seasonal ratio applied to the July 2026 level

methods.rationale: Anchors on the latest observed monthly total (July 2026, p16) and applies a September/July seasonal ratio. Failure mode: if the July level is a summer peak that September does not revert from, the estimate is biased low; the assumption range covers this.

methods.label: m3

p148.role: Total A&E attendances, England, September 2025 (all types)

a1.role: Year-on-year growth factor for September 2026 vs September 2025

methods.rationale: Direct seasonal analogue: last September's observed total (p148) times a YoY growth factor grounded in recent 2-3% growth (p2, p18, p7). Failure mode: September 2025 was an unusually high base (+7% YoY), so growth may undershoot; range spans flat to +7%.

methods.label: m4

p94.role: Average daily A&E attendances, England, June 2026 (81,264 per day)

a3.role: September 2026 daily-rate uplift vs June 2026 daily average

methods.rationale: Physical-flow route: June 2026 record daily average (p94) times 30 days in September times a small seasonal adjustment. Failure mode: June is a summer peak and September may be materially lower; the assumption range and the 30-day calendar constant handle this. Independent of the monthly-total routes.

weight_basis.m2: B1 of 3 blocks; median of blocks: not the median (one vote, counts in the interval)
weight_basis.m3: B2 of 3 blocks; median of blocks: not the median (one vote, counts in the interval)
weight_basis.m4: B3 of 3 blocks; median of blocks: this block is the median

combination.weight_gate: off: inverse backtest-error weights need a bank-level gate (>= 30 scored questions with >= 2 backtested routes, hit rate >= 0.7; METHODS_ZH 4.1), which has not been run

m3.note: Monte Carlo width below the default, not used to narrow

interval.rule: several blocks: root mean square of the block widths, times the Birge ratio when it exceeds 1

baseline.rule: seasonal naive: the target's value for the same calendar period last year

kept.name: September 2026 vs September 2025 growth factor
kept.rationale: Recent YoY growth: April 2026 +2.1% (p2), July 2026 +3.3% (p18). September 2025 was itself +7% (p149), so a repeat of that surge is unlikely; centre near 2.5% with a range spanning flat to +7%.
kept.applies_when: September 2026 demand grows at roughly the recent 2-3% annual pace with no new shock.
kept.falsified_by: Evidence of a large autumn 2026 demand surge (e.g. early-September daily figures well above 2025) or a major service disruption.

kept.name: September-to-July seasonal ratio
kept.rationale: September is typically slightly below the July/August summer peak. September 2025 2.31m vs July 2025 ~2.41m (implied by p16/p18) gives ~0.96; September 2023 2.166m vs July 2023 ~2.1m gives ~1.03. Centre ~0.94 reflecting a modest post-summer dip.
kept.applies_when: September 2026 follows the normal post-summer seasonal pattern relative to July 2026.
kept.falsified_by: Evidence that September 2026 is unusually busy (e.g. early-September daily rates at or above July's).

kept.name: September 2026 daily-rate uplift vs June 2026 daily average
kept.rationale: June 2026 daily average 81,264 (p94) is a summer peak; September daily rates are typically a few percent lower. September 2025 2.31m/30 = 77,000/day vs June 2025 ~74,000/day suggests September can be higher, but 2026 June was a record. Centre slightly below June.
kept.applies_when: September 2026 daily throughput is close to but slightly below the June 2026 record daily rate.
kept.falsified_by: Early-September 2026 daily figures showing rates well above 81,264.

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.

The magnitude gate (v2.15d) asks the model once, without retrieval, for a rough estimate; whether the evidence-based estimate is more than 2x above or below it can carry the model's memory of the target into one repair. The rough number itself never enters a computation or a prompt; the estimate before that repair is kept in judge_rounds[-1].magnitude_checks[0]. The gate is off in the own-history ablation.
